opp_002:n1.prompt: You are helping me onboard a new 1099 contractor in {{vendor}}, our payroll platform, so they can be paid and issued a 1099 at year-end. If you don't already have it, ask me for: the contractor's full legal name, email address, mailing address, business type (individual/LLC/etc.), Tax ID or SSN (only confirm it's on file, don't ask me to paste it directly), start date, payment rate/schedule, and which {{vendor}} account/workspace (domain or org identifier) to use. Also confirm you have configured credentials for {{vendor}}'s API or CLI. Once you have the required details: 1) Authenticate to {{vendor}} using my configured credentials. 2) Use {{vendor}}'s documented contractor-creation API or CLI command to create the contractor record with the details provided, setting contractor type to 1099 and configuring compensation/payment schedule as specified. 3) Verify the record was created successfully by retrieving it back from {{vendor}} and checking that name, contact info, and payment terms match what I gave you. 4) If {{vendor}} requires a W-9 or tax form to be uploaded or e-signed by the contractor, note this and flag that this remains a human step for the contractor to complete themselves. Done looks like: a contractor record exists in {{vendor}} with correct identity, address, compensation, and 1099 classification, ready to be paid. Report back to me with: the contractor's name, the record/contractor ID created in {{vendor}}, a summary of the compensation/payment setup, confirmation the record verified correctly, and any outstanding items (like pending W-9 submission) that still need contractor or human action.

opp_002:n2.prompt: You are helping me complete step opp_002:n2 in onboarding a new 1099 contractor: getting the contractor to submit their own W-9 and bank/direct-deposit details through our payroll system. Please ask me for anything you need: the contractor's full name and email address, and confirmation of which payroll platform we use (e.g., Gusto, QuickBooks Payroll, Rippling, etc.) since I already have configured credentials for it. Then: 1) Log into our payroll platform using my configured credentials and locate the contractor-onboarding or 'add contractor' flow. 2) Create the contractor record with the name/email I gave you, and trigger the platform's standard invitation so the contractor receives a self-service link to submit their W-9 tax information and bank account details directly. 3) Confirm the invitation was sent successfully and note the contractor's status (e.g., 'invited', 'pending'). Because only the contractor holds their own SSN/EIN and banking details, actually filling out and submitting the W-9 and bank form remains a human step that only the contractor can perform on their own timeline — you cannot do this for them. Your job is to prepare and send the invite, then periodically check (poll) the platform for a status change to 'completed' or 'verified.' Report back to me with: the date you sent the invite, the contractor's current status each time you check, and a clear alert once the status shows the W-9 and bank details have been submitted so we can proceed to the next onboarding step.

opp_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me verify that a 1099 contractor is payable in {{vendor}}, our payroll platform, before I run their next payment. I'll give you the contractor's name or email if you need it to locate their record — ask me if it's missing.

Please do the following using our {{vendor}} account with your configured credentials:
1. Look up the contractor's profile in {{vendor}} (via the dashboard or documented API) and check whether a completed W-9 is on file. Note the status (submitted/signed, pending, or missing).
2. Check whether a valid payment method (e.g., bank account for direct deposit) is set up and active for this contractor.
3. If {{vendor}} offers a preview or validation call for contractor payments, use it to surface any submission blockers (missing tax info, no payment method, incomplete profile, etc.) before an actual payment is attempted.
4. Compile a short status report listing: W-9 status, payment method status, and any blockers returned by the validation check.

If the W-9 is missing or unsigned, or no payment method is on file, do not attempt to trigger collection or send new onboarding documents yourself — flag exactly what's missing and stop for human sign-off so I can decide whether to send a reminder or self-serve onboarding link to the contractor.

If everything checks out (W-9 on file, payment method active, no blockers), confirm to me that the contractor is fully payable and ready for their next payroll run.

Report back with: contractor name, W-9 status, payment method status, any blocker messages from the validation check, and a clear yes/no on whether they are currently payable.
